payload.description:
Goal: Extract OpenClaw context management behind a pluggable core abstraction while preserving current behavior.

Scope:
- Define a neutral, OpenClaw-native context execution contract (no LCM-specific APIs in core).
- Route runtime context execution through that contract:
  - ingest
  - assemble
  - compact
- Re-implement current behavior via a legacy/default engine implementation using the new abstraction.
- Keep existing compaction UX/event contracts intact (/compact behavior, auto-compaction signaling, compaction counters).

Non-goals:
- No mandatory retrieval/lineage semantics in core interface.
- No behavior changes for users unless explicitly behind config/feature selection.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Existing context behavior is preserved when default engine is selected.
2) Existing tests remain in place and passing.
3) New tests are added for abstraction boundaries and engine selection behavior.
4) A plugin-capable selection path exists for alternate context engines.
payload.title: Core: pluggable context management abstraction + legacy reimplementation

payload.description:

Acceptance criteria:

- Unit tests cover selection/fallback behavior.

payload.description:
Goal: Implement Lossless Context Management (LCM) as a plugin-backed context engine on top of the new pluggable context system.

Scope:
- Implement LCM ingestion/assembly/compaction in plugin engine form.
- Implement retrieval/introspection surfaces (describe/grep/expand) outside core engine contract.
- Implement subagent expansion strategy:
  - main agent routes via describe/grep
  - subagent performs bounded deep expand traversal
  - main agent receives distilled findings
- Enforce secure cross-session expansion authorization.
- Evaluate sqlite-first implementation in place of embedded postgres when practical.

Acceptance criteria:
1) LCM runs as selectable context engine plugin.
2) Expansion strategy with subagents is implemented and tested.
3) Security controls prevent unauthorized cross-session expansion.
4) Storage decision documented with sqlite-first feasibility and tradeoffs.
5) Existing OpenClaw tests remain passing; new LCM tests added.
payload.title: LCM plugin: implement lossless context engine + subagent expansion

payload.description:
Add secure cross-session expansion handoff and authorization controls.

Security concerns to address:
- Child subagent must not expand arbitrary IDs outside authorized scope.
- Expansion permissions must be bound to explicit conversation/session scope.
- Enforce depth/token/ID bounds from main-agent handoff.

Deliverables:
- Scoped expansion grant model (or equivalent authorization mechanism).
- Validation in retrieval endpoints before expansion execution.
- Negative tests for unauthorized cross-session access.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unauthorized expansion attempts are rejected.
- Only explicitly delegated scopes can be traversed by subagents.

payload.description:
Goal: Extract OpenClaw context management behind a pluggable core abstraction while preserving current behavior.

Current implementation context (must be understood before edits):
- Context assembly and message replacement are currently wired inside `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.ts`.
- Auto-compaction orchestration is currently wired inside `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.ts`.
- Manual compaction path is wired through `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compact.ts` and `/compact` handling in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts`.
- Plugin system exists (`src/plugins/*`), but there is no first-class context-engine registration path yet.

Scope:
- Define a neutral, OpenClaw-native context execution contract (no LCM-specific semantics in required core methods).
- Route runtime context execution through that contract:
  - ingest
  - assemble
  - compact
- Re-implement current behavior via a legacy/default engine implementation using the new abstraction.
- Keep existing compaction UX/event contracts intact:
  - stream events from `src/agents/pi-embedded-subscribe.handlers.lifecycle.ts`
  - session compaction counts and status behavior used in auto-reply/session updates

Non-goals:
- No mandatory retrieval/lineage/expand APIs in the required core interface.
- No user-visible behavior regressions unless explicitly behind selection config.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Existing behavior is preserved with default legacy engine selected.
2) Existing tests remain in place and passing.
3) New tests are added for abstraction boundaries and engine selection/fallback.
4) A plugin-capable selection path exists for alternate context engines.

Define `ContextEngine` core contract and selection model.

Implementation context:
- Current plugin slot system is defined in `src/plugins/slots.ts` and `src/plugins/config-state.ts` (today only memory slot exists).
- Plugin API/registration plumbing is in `src/plugins/types.ts`, `src/plugins/registry.ts`, and `src/plugins/loader.ts`.

Deliverables:
- New core execution contract with required methods only: ingest/assemble/compact.
- Engine registry/selection mechanism with default legacy engine.
- Config surface for selecting active context engine (slot or equivalent), including schema and validation wiring.

Constraints:
- Required core contract must remain neutral and not require retrieval/lineage methods.
- Selection must default to legacy behavior when unset/invalid.

Acceptance criteria:
- Contract is neutral (no lineage/retrieval required methods).
- Selection defaults to legacy behavior.
- Unit tests cover selection, invalid selection, and fallback behavior.

Rewire runtime context paths to call `ContextEngine` instead of direct inline orchestration.

Primary callsites to rewire:
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.ts` (context assembly path before prompt)
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run.ts` (overflow-triggered auto-compaction/retry path)
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compact.ts` (manual/direct compaction path)
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-compact.ts` (/compact command path)

Behavioral constraints:
- Do not break compaction stream event semantics used by lifecycle handlers.
- Preserve session compaction count and status integration.
- Preserve current error handling/retry semantics for overflow + compaction failure paths.

Acceptance criteria:
- No direct compaction orchestration in these callsites bypassing engine contract.
- Existing user-visible behavior remains equivalent with legacy engine.
- Existing tests continue passing; add regression tests for rewired call paths.

Implement `LegacyContextEngine` that reproduces current OpenClaw behavior via the new interface.

Implementation context:
- Legacy compaction/summarization helpers currently live in `src/agents/compaction.ts`.
- Embedded runner history sanitization/truncation logic is in `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.ts` and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/compact.ts`.

Deliverables:
- Legacy adapter that preserves current ingest/assemble/compact outcomes.
- Adapter behavior parity for compaction summaries, token estimates, and retry expectations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Parity validated against existing tests.
- Compaction event and counter semantics remain compatible.
- No behavior regression for `/compact`, overflow auto-compaction, and follow-up status surfaces.

Add plugin registration path for pluggable context engines with safe startup behavior.

Implementation context:
- Plugin registration points: `src/plugins/types.ts`, `src/plugins/registry.ts`, `src/plugins/loader.ts`.
- Existing plugin runtime/tool resolution: `src/plugins/tools.ts`, `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts`.

Deliverables:
- Plugin API surface that allows a plugin to provide a `ContextEngine` implementation.
- Startup validation and diagnostics for missing/invalid engine implementations.
- Deterministic fallback to legacy engine when plugin engine cannot load.

Constraints:
- Keep plugin registration additive; do not break existing plugin APIs.
- Failure modes must be explicit in diagnostics/logging.

Acceptance criteria:
- Alternate engine can be selected and loaded without touching runtime callsites.
- Invalid/missing plugin engine falls back safely to legacy engine.
- Tests cover registration, selection, and fallback diagnostics.

Testing and migration hardening for pluggable context architecture.

Implementation context:
- Existing compaction/runner coverage includes tests under `src/agents/*compaction*.test.ts` and overflow/embedded runner tests (including `run.overflow-compaction` coverage).
- Session/status flows depend on compaction counters and lifecycle behavior.

Deliverables:
- Preserve existing coverage and passing tests (do not remove current tests).
- Add abstraction-focused tests:
  - engine contract behavior
  - default engine selection
  - invalid engine fallback
  - legacy parity checkpoints
- Add migration notes for maintainers implementing future engines.

Acceptance criteria:
- CI-equivalent suite remains green.
- New tests prevent regressions in engine selection and parity.
- Migration notes explain how to add a new engine safely.

Goal: Implement Lossless Context Management (LCM) as a plugin-backed context engine on top of the pluggable context system from `openclaw-c3a`.

Prerequisite:
- `openclaw-c3a` must land first (LCM epic depends on it).

Scope:
- Implement LCM ingestion/assembly/compaction in plugin engine form.
- Keep retrieval/introspection adapters (`describe/grep/expand`) outside required core engine methods.
- Implement subagent expansion strategy from updated LCM docs:
  - main agent routes via describe/grep to target IDs
  - subagent performs bounded deep expand traversal
  - main agent receives distilled findings and cited IDs
- Enforce secure cross-session expansion authorization.
- Evaluate sqlite-first backend vs embedded postgres.

Critical OpenClaw integration context:
- Subagent spawning/model override path is in `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts`.
- Subagent announce/return flow is in `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`.
- Existing session scoping/filtering (`spawnedBy`) behavior is in `src/gateway/sessions-resolve.ts` and `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`.

Acceptance criteria:
1) LCM runs as selectable context engine plugin.
2) Subagent expansion strategy is implemented and tested.
3) Security controls prevent unauthorized cross-session expansion.
4) Storage decision documented with sqlite-first feasibility and tradeoffs.
5) Existing OpenClaw tests remain passing; new LCM tests added.

Decide and implement LCM storage backend with sqlite-first evaluation.

Required decision context:
- LCM spec currently describes PostgreSQL schema/locking semantics.
- OpenClaw/plugin deployment ergonomics may favor sqlite for local/in-process operation.

Deliverables:
- Technical decision record comparing sqlite vs embedded postgres for v1.
- If sqlite chosen: schema design, migration approach, and concurrency/locking strategy.
- If sqlite cannot meet requirements, document exact blockers and define fallback plan.

Evaluation criteria to include:
- transaction semantics for lineage writes
- lock contention/retry behavior
- indexing/search feasibility for grep/full-text
- operational complexity in typical OpenClaw installs

Acceptance criteria:
- Decision and rationale are explicit and reproducible.
- Chosen backend implemented for local dev path.

Implement LCM `ConversationStore` + ingestion pipeline in plugin engine.

Implementation context:
- Ingestion must capture canonical data for messages/tool results/file artifacts.
- OpenClaw transcript/tool lifecycle touchpoints include session manager and tool-result persistence paths in `src/agents/session-tool-result-guard-wrapper.ts` and embedded runner flows.

Deliverables:
- Canonical message/part persistence.
- Summary/lineage/context-item persistence primitives.
- Idempotent ingest behavior and deterministic ordering guarantees.

Constraints:
- Canonical layer is append-first and non-destructive.
- No data-loss on write path.

Acceptance criteria:
- Invariants validated with tests.
- Canonical persistence supports downstream assemble/compact/retrieval flows.

Implement LCM `ContextAssembler` + `CompactionEngine` in plugin engine.

Implementation context:
- This task is the plugin implementation behind core engine contract methods.
- It must integrate with rewired runtime callsites from `openclaw-c3a` without bespoke branching.

Deliverables:
- Budget-aware context assembly.
- Leaf and condensed compaction passes.
- Safety rules: fresh-tail protection, non-destructive compaction, ordering invariants.

Constraints:
- Preserve OpenClaw runtime expectations for compaction outcomes and retry behavior.
- Ensure concurrent compaction safety and no partial lineage states.

Acceptance criteria:
- Compaction reduces active context on fixture conversations.
- Concurrent safety covered by tests.

Expose LCM retrieval/introspection as plugin-owned adapters (not required core engine methods).

Implementation context:
- Plugin tools can be registered via `api.registerTool` (`src/plugins/types.ts`, `src/plugins/tools.ts`).
- Plugin gateway methods can be registered via `api.registerGatewayMethod` (`src/plugins/registry.ts`).

Deliverables:
- `describe`/`grep`/`expand` adapters via plugin tools and/or gateway methods.
- Bounded traversal controls (depth, token cap, limits).
- Explicit split between summary-id expansion and file-id handling.

Constraints:
- Adapter layer must not own compaction/lineage core rules.
- Retrieval APIs must be auditable and bounded.

Acceptance criteria:
- Retrieval works without extending required core `ContextEngine` contract.
- Adapter behavior is validated by tests.

Implement subagent-driven LCM expansion orchestration per updated strategy.

Implementation context:
- Subagent spawning is implemented by `sessions_spawn` in `src/agents/tools/sessions-spawn-tool.ts`.
- Child model can be explicitly controlled via spawn `model` parameter and defaults.
- Subagent return/announcement behavior is managed in `src/agents/subagent-announce.ts`.

Deliverables:
- Main-agent routing pass to identify candidate IDs via describe/grep.
- Subagent deep expansion passes with explicit depth/token bounds.
- Distilled return payloads with cited IDs for iterative follow-up.
- Deterministic control over subagent model selection for expansion runs.

Constraints:
- Avoid flooding top-level context with raw expansion payloads.
- Preserve auditability via cited IDs for follow-up traversal.

Acceptance criteria:
- Multi-hop traversal is delegated to subagents, not main-agent prompt bloat.
- Iterative pass behavior is covered by tests.

Add secure cross-session expansion handoff and authorization controls.

Implementation context:
- Cross-session resolution and spawned-session scoping behavior exists in:
  - `src/gateway/sessions-resolve.ts`
  - `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`
- LCM retrieval endpoints/tools must enforce equivalent or stronger scope checks.

Security concerns to address:
- Child subagent must not expand arbitrary IDs outside delegated scope.
- Expansion permissions must bind to explicit conversation/session scope.
- Enforce main-agent handoff bounds (IDs/depth/token caps/expiry).

Deliverables:
- Scoped expansion grant model (or equivalent authorization mechanism).
- Validation in retrieval endpoints/tools before expansion execution.
- Negative tests for unauthorized cross-session access and out-of-scope IDs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unauthorized expansion attempts are rejected.
- Only explicitly delegated scopes can be traversed by subagents.

Implement LCM integrity checker and observability.

Implementation context:
- LCM requires lineage/integrity invariants and operational metrics.
- Plugin background workers/services can be hosted through plugin service registration.

Deliverables:
- Integrity scan/report and repair-plan generation.
- Metrics/logging for:
  - context tokens
  - compaction runs/summaries
  - expand/search latency
  - integrity failures

Acceptance criteria:
- Integrity failures are detectable and actionable.
- Operational metrics/logs are available to validate steady-state health.

Create end-to-end and regression coverage for LCM plugin on pluggable context engine.

Implementation context:
- Existing OpenClaw compaction and runner coverage must remain in place.
- New LCM paths must be tested alongside legacy engine compatibility.

Deliverables:
- Integration tests for ingest -> assemble -> compact -> retrieve/expand.
- Subagent expansion tests verifying routing vs deep traversal separation.
- Security regression tests for cross-session authorization constraints.
- Backward compatibility tests ensuring legacy/default engine behavior still passes.

Acceptance criteria:
- Existing test coverage remains passing and preserved.
- New tests cover LCM behavior, subagent strategy, and security controls.
